index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a methodological framework for evaluating fisheries management policies using reinforcement learning and comparative policy analysis. It is divided into three main parts: (a) a feedback loop diagram of the decision-making process, (b) three distinct utility scenarios for policy evaluation, and (c) a legend defining four types of management policies.

Part (a) illustrates a closed-loop system where a 'Policy' module, represented by a blue human head icon inside a rounded rectangle, receives observations and outputs an action. The policy module contains a simple U vs. Obs. graph indicating utility as a function of observation. The action, labeled 'U exploitation rate' and accompanied by a fishing hook icon, is directed toward an 'Age-structured fish stock' module, depicted as a rounded rectangle containing four blue fish icons of varying sizes. This fish stock module feeds back two observations—'Vulnerable biomass' and 'Mean fish weight'—to the policy module via an intermediate 'Observations' box, which includes icons of a fishing hook and a scale. The arrows form a continuous cycle, indicating real-time adaptive decision-making.

Part (b) outlines three utility scenarios under which policies are evaluated. Scenario 1, 'Yield utility,' defines utility as total yield, symbolized by a single fish icon. Scenario 2, 'HARA utility,' represents risk-averse harvest behavior, shown with a fishing boat icon. Scenario 3, 'Trophy fishing,' defines utility as the yield of large, trophy-sized fish, illustrated by two fish icons—one marked with a red 'X' (small fish) and one with a green checkmark (large fish).

Part (c) provides a legend for four policy types. 'Const. U' is represented by a blue open book icon and describes a constant fishing exploitation rate U* that maximizes long-term utility, based on maximum sustainable yield theory [Hilborn & Walters, 1992]. 'Precautionary Policy' uses a blue triangle with an exclamation mark and refers to a rectilinear control rule based on biomass reference points, introduced in [Walters, 1975] and widely used today [DFO, 2009]. '1-Observation ML' and '2-Observation ML' are both represented by blue robot icons and denote neural-network policies optimized via reinforcement learning; the former depends on 1000s of parameters using only total caught biomass, while the latter additionally incorporates mean fish weight observation [Lapeyrolerie et al., 2022; Montealegre-Mora et al., 2023]. All icons are rendered in blue, and all text is black, with clear, bold labels for each module and scenario. The layout is clean and modular, emphasizing the flow from policy to stock to observation and back, with side-by-side comparison of utility functions and policy types.
